source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: stop a running process (Ctrl-C) and confirm it stopped
experience: Stopping a process needs an interrupt key in the right terminal and a check of what it printed; closing the tab or pkill is wrong.

setup.name: watcher
setup.run: bash -c 'trap "echo watcher stopped, code $((1000+337)); exit 0" INT TERM; echo watching src/ for changes; while :; do sleep 1; done'

prompt: Stop the watcher on my right. What did it say when it stopped?

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: find which tab runs a program among several
experience: The agent must look at what each tab runs (process or screen) before acting on one, not guess by position.
prompt: One of the tabs on my right is running tail. Rename that one to follow.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: two tabs with the same name (ambiguity)
experience: Two tabs are both named server; reading only the first and answering with one port is wrong.
prompt: What port is my server tab on?

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: server in one tab, curl in another, read the result
experience: The agent must read the server's port from its screen, run curl in a new tab beside it, wait, and report the body.
prompt: My dev server is running in the tab on my right. Curl /hello.txt from it in a new tab next to it and tell me what comes back.

experience: Several steps: create a named workspace without focus, move exactly the test tabs (same terminals), keep the server tab here.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: group three named tabs, not the fourth

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: rename every tab in a pane by its command
experience: The agent must inspect each of three tabs and rename each after its own program, not one or by guess.
prompt: Name the tabs on my right after what's running in each.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: close only the tabs whose command finished
experience: The agent must tell idle shells from running programs and close only the idle ones.
prompt: Close the tabs on my right whose commands already finished. Keep the ones still running.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: sidebar status set, wait, clear
experience: Set a status, run work on the right, wait for it, then clear the status; agents forget the clear or skip the wait.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30; mined #34/#35 (sleep then read, busy poll)
experience: A 10 s script: the agent must wait for it to end and read its exit code, not sleep-and-read or answer early.
prompt: Run `bash slow.sh` in a new tab next to my shell on the right and tell me its exit code when it finishes.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: one value 600+ lines up in a background tab's history
experience: The answer is one line among 1500 in a tab that is not the active one; the visible screen and a short history read miss it.

setup.name: build
setup.run: for i in $(seq 1 1500); do if [ $i -eq 873 ]; then echo "ERROR E$((i*3)) disk quota"; else echo "compiled unit $i"; fi; done

prompt: Somewhere way up in the build tab on my right there's one ERROR line. What's the code?

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: split down from the agent's own pane when asked
experience: Asked for a terminal underneath, the agent must split its own pane downward, not right and not a tab.
prompt: Give me a terminal underneath this one and run `echo EVAL_BELOW_OK` in it.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: do not type into a busy terminal
experience: The right terminal runs a long job; typing the command there queues it behind the job (or interrupts it). It needs its own tab.
prompt: My long job's running on the right. Run `echo EVAL_SIDE_OK` somewhere I can see it, without stopping the job.

source: hard cases r13 2026-10-30: conditional action on a read result (overcorrection guard for notify)
experience: The checks pass, so no notification: the agent must read the result before acting on the condition.

setup.name: shell
setup.run: printf '%s\n' 'for c in lint types unit e2e; do echo "$c: ok"; sleep 1; done' 'echo "$((2+2)) of 4 checks passed"' > check.sh

prompt: Run `bash check.sh` in a new tab next to my shell on the right; ping me with a cmux notification only if any check fails.
